problem_meta.agent_answer:
## Reaction identification

The reaction is **acidic deprotection of a tert-butyl ester to a carboxylic acid**:

\[
\mathrm{RCO_2C(CH_3)_3 \rightarrow RCO_2H}
\]

The large heteroaromatic/chiral scaffold remains unchanged; the tert-butyl ester group is removed.

## Recommended reagent

**Hydrogen chloride in acetonitrile**

- Reagent: **HCl**, commonly as a solution in dioxane or another suitable solvent
- Solvent: **acetonitrile**
- Approximate time from the matching records: **1 hour**
- Reported yield in the closest records: **98.9%**
- Temperature: **not reported**, so avoid treating any specific temperature as database-supported

A practical starting condition would be:

> Treat the tert-butyl ester with HCl in acetonitrile, monitor disappearance of the ester, then remove solvent and isolate the carboxylic acid, optionally after neutralization or precipitation.

## Other plausible reagents

| Reagent/condition | Typical use |
|---|---|
| **TFA in dichloromethane** | Common mild-to-moderate tert-butyl ester cleavage |
| **HCl in dioxane** | Standard acidolytic removal of tert-butyl esters |
| **HCl in ethyl acetate or isopropanol** | Alternative convenient HCl sources |
| **Methanesulfonic acid** | Strong acid alternative; use cautiously |
| **Triflic acid** | Very strong alternative, generally excessive unless the substrate is highly resistant |

## Best choice

Use **HCl in acetonitrile** first because it is the closest condition supported by the retrieved reaction records (`call_jvREo1j8pUrE3SDTIXvg68SB`). The database evidence indicates duplicated records reporting **98.9% yield after 1 hour**, but does not specify the exact HCl concentration or temperature.
